findings: publish() explicitly admits an existing owned draft: same tag, prerelease=true and exact source marker. It does not require its body to equal the full notes. The reserved tag must still be a commit pointing to the exact source; it is never moved or deleted.

Original main() local preflight remains mandatory. The draft path uploads, downloads and verifies the exact 25-asset inventory, checksum completeness, producer bytes, scanner/Python/compiler/service/native evidence and source/profile semantics, then rechecks the tag before its publication PATCH.

The workflow copies the COMPLETE notes unchanged as the expected asset and includes it in SHA256SUMS.txt. Draft readback compares its digest to the producer. The 898-byte overview body changes no source, tag, expected asset, scanner/review record or gate.

After publication PATCH, publish() reads back ownership/tag/prerelease/draft metadata and rechecks the tag. Asset verification precedes PATCH; already-published reuse calls verify(false). No recovery-specific shortcut.

limits.scope: Static source/data compatibility only; no current installed/native/final-combined/publication approval. Authenticate any actual owned draft, then retain every original publisher and final-consumer gate. No manual publication or waiver.
